clue.text: Woosnam's first or last golfer with wrong-handed clubs to get famous jug

indicators.note: first says only the opening letter of the golfer's surname Woosnam is used

parts.note: Ian Woosnam, the Welsh golfer, whose surname supplies both its first and its last letter

indicators.note: last says the closing letter of the same surname Woosnam is taken too

parts.note: Tiger Woods, the American golfer

indicators.note: wrong-handed swaps left for right: the L (left) in clubs is replaced by R (right)

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A golfing tale: Woosnam or some other player using clubs made for the wrong hand.
explanation.walkthrough: W and M are the first and last letters of Woosnam. 'Wrong-handed' turns the L (left) of CLUBS into R (right), giving CRUBS. Jug is British slang for prison; Wormwood Scrubs is a well-known London jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Wormwood Scrubs is a notorious London prison, and jug is old slang for a jail.

explanation.definitionFit: A warmonger stirs up conflict, so it is a fair word for an aggressor.

explanation.definitionFit: An opium den was a place where people went to smoke the drug.

explanation.definitionFit: To stand down is to quit a post, the same as having resigned.

clue.text: Newspaper describes America's Got Talent's big characters for the commoners
